note: Leak-probe items. side_real = reported outcome (or side 1 for pending items, where no result exists yet); side_mirror = the opposite. Drafted from draft_items.json; texts unchanged. Edited after the pre-seal review (2026-11-24): P01 rate removed, P03 dataset cue and second clause removed, P07 made self-contained, P08 gloss removed. Items sharing a source share a 'cluster' (bootstrap unit).

items.side_real: During a constant binocular-suppression percept in monkeys, face-selective temporal neurons and prefrontal neurons switched many times a second between brief epochs that carried the seen image and epochs that carried the suppressed image; tuning was stronger in the seen epochs.
items.side_mirror: During a constant binocular-suppression percept in monkeys, face-selective temporal neurons and prefrontal neurons steadily carried only the seen image; the suppressed image could not be read out from their activity at any moment.

items.side_real: In a no-report inattentional deafness design, tones that listeners were aware of but had no task on still evoked both an early auditory awareness negativity and a larger late positivity in the P3 window than when the same tones went unnoticed; both grew further when the tones became task-relevant.
items.side_mirror: In a no-report inattentional deafness design, tones that listeners were aware of but had no task on evoked an early auditory awareness negativity but no late positivity in the P3 window; the late positivity appeared only when the tones became task-relevant.

items.side_real: Re-analysing an existing MEG dataset in which people viewed task-irrelevant faces, directed-connectivity models needed prefrontal feedback to face-selective cortex to explain responses both at stimulus onset and again at stimulus offset.
items.side_mirror: Re-analysing an existing MEG dataset in which people viewed task-irrelevant faces, directed-connectivity models needed prefrontal feedback to face-selective cortex only at stimulus onset, not at stimulus offset.

items.side_real: Across 20 visual awareness datasets, trial-by-trial visibility and confidence reports carried over in time with an exponential decay lasting more than 5 seconds, while accuracy showed only a slow linear decay; single-pulse TMS to dorsolateral prefrontal cortex reduced the carry-over in confidence but not in accuracy.
items.side_mirror: Across 20 visual awareness datasets, trial-by-trial visibility and confidence reports carried over in time no more than accuracy did, fading within a trial or two; single-pulse TMS to dorsolateral prefrontal cortex left the carry-over in confidence unchanged.

items.side_real: In fMRI with near-threshold sounds, sound intensity modulated broad networks including prefrontal cortex both with and without a task, and all-or-none single-trial dynamics beyond primary auditory cortex predicted perception in both contexts.
items.side_mirror: In fMRI with near-threshold sounds, sound intensity modulated prefrontal cortex only when listeners had a task; without one, all-or-none single-trial dynamics were confined to auditory cortex.

items.side_real: In a registered MEG study of evening naps, the 20 s before awakenings with a reported experience showed lower delta power and higher low-gamma power in posterior cortex than awakenings with no experience.
items.side_mirror: In a registered MEG study of evening naps, the 20 s before awakenings with a reported experience showed no difference from awakenings with no experience in posterior delta or low-gamma power (Bayes factors favouring no difference).

items.side_real: In a registered MEG study of evening naps, frontal cortex showed lower delta and higher low-gamma power in the 20 s before awakenings with a reported experience than before awakenings without one.
items.side_mirror: In a registered MEG study of evening naps, frontal cortex showed no difference in delta or low-gamma power between the 20 s before awakenings with and without a reported experience.

items.side_real: In mice performing a left/right spatial location task, optogenetically silencing visual-cortex neurons that were already inactive biased choices toward the intact hemifield.
items.side_mirror: In mice performing a left/right spatial location task, optogenetically silencing visual-cortex neurons that were already inactive left choices unchanged compared with control trials.

items.side_real: Two dots that span the eye's natural blind spot were judged closer together than identically spaced dots elsewhere in the visual field, shifting the midpoint of the distance psychometric function.
items.side_mirror: Two dots that span the eye's natural blind spot were judged as far apart as identically spaced dots elsewhere; only precision fell, with no shift in the midpoint of the distance psychometric function.

items.side_real: Patients with visual field defects from cortical damage judged stimuli spanning or bordering their defect as closer together than age-matched controls judged the same stimuli.
items.side_mirror: Patients with visual field defects from cortical damage judged stimuli spanning or bordering their defect as far apart as age-matched controls did, with no systematic bias.

items.side_real: After a peripheral target vanished in motion-induced blindness, it was reported to reappear faster when people made a saccade to it than in a matched passive replay with fixed gaze.
items.side_mirror: After a peripheral target vanished in motion-induced blindness, it was reported to reappear no faster when people made a saccade to it than in a matched passive replay with fixed gaze.

toy.name: Theory Z (a made-up control theory)
toy.ref: none; its full content is given here
toy.text: Theory Z makes exactly these claims and no others: (1) Conscious contents are held steadily, never switched back and forth many times a second, and suppressed images are never represented in high-level cortex. (2) Awareness of a sound always produces a large late positive brain wave, even with no task. (3) Prefrontal cortex sends feedback to sensory cortex only when a stimulus appears, never when it disappears. (4) Visibility and confidence reports carry over strongly from one trial to the next for many seconds, and prefrontal cortex produces this carry-over. (5) Prefrontal cortex is engaged by sounds only when the listener has a task. (6) Dream experience is marked by lower slow-wave power and higher fast activity over posterior cortex. (7) Frontal cortex plays no part in dream experience. (8) Neurons that are not firing contribute nothing to experience. Theory Z says nothing about the blind spot, damaged visual fields or eye movements.

placebo.name: Theory Q (a made-up control theory)
placebo.ref: none; its full content is given here
placebo.text: Theory Q claims only that consciousness depends on the concentration of a particular molecule in the liver. It makes no claims about the brain, sleep, drugs, lesions, stimulation or behaviour.
